summary: All four occurrences checked. Retain senses 1-2 and the existing English gloss for 2; German quotations remain edition text.
The new explicit-n forms address a specific uncertainty in the old heading, without proving that the older n-less leaning example belongs to the same lexeme.

qm marks the opposed group or adverse condition; endurance can also occur without an expressed opponent. These data support intransitive endure, not the unattested transitive English component 'support'.
The borrowing entry dyn 1 is not implicated by these contexts; no homonym merge is proposed.
Does mdayalle 'lean/stay' at 29/403 belong to dayan- with assimilation, or to dwr as the old heading suggests?
Is transitive 'support' in inherited II.2 independently attested? The supplied examples establish endurance only.
How should source emphatic ḍ in JTM compare with d in 91/44 and the inherited base forms?
Endurance applies both to people holding out against attackers and to birds exposed to weather; no new participant sense.
